correctness.rationale: The bounded categorical summands have uniformly bounded fourth moments for their normalized centered sums (the fourth-moment expansion is O(N²) before scaling). The cyclic functional is continuous and at most 6 times the maximum coordinate magnitude, so its first two moments converge by uniform integrability even when the Gaussian covariance is singular. Coupling the Gaussian through the positive square root of diag(p)−ppᵀ gives simplex continuity. With three coordinates the statistic is twice the range, giving full permutation invariance. On the symmetric line S=Z₁−Z₃ and M=−3Z₂ have variances 2a and 18a(1−2a) and zero covariance; their independence and the identity |(M+S)/2|+|(M−S)/2|=max(|M|,|S|) give the stated polar integrand. Its first and second angular moments give the stated profile. As an independent symbolic route, forming the covariance of the three contrasts and using pairwise Gaussian absolute-value covariances gives V(u)=1.052263614148347, V′(1/3)=0, V″(1/3)=3(81−16π−24√3)/π≈−10.34637812770789, and V(b)=4(1−2/π)≈1.453520910529675. The Gaussian density restricted to the fixed tangent plane is positive definite near u; parameter derivatives of its first two range moments are dominated on a smaller neighborhood by a polynomial times a common Gaussian tail. Thus the Taylor Hessian exists, permutation symmetry makes it scalar on the tangent plane, and ‖(1,−2,1)‖²=6 converts the ray second derivative to the stated coefficient by division by 12. Since b majorizes u and gives a larger value, Schur concavity fails; nearby nonuniform vectors also majorize u but give smaller values, ruling out Schur convexity. The segment drops below both endpoint values before reaching b, violating quasi-concavity and forcing a minimum strictly between the two endpoints.
residual_risks: This is a limiting variance for fixed p with category-matched centering. It does not address finite-sample optimality, probabilities changing with N, or the location or uniqueness of any global maximizer.

evidence: The cyclic paper's uniform limit in Theorem 3.1 applies at fixed bin count n≥3, not just n≥5. Its nonuniform matched formula Proposition 5.4 has n≥5. Part 4 gives an open-chain Gaussian variance formula reaching n=3 as well as classical successive-difference precedents.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Uniform Theorem 3.1 covers the uniform baseline as a genuine special case. The higher-bin cyclic formula does not apply as stated to n=3, and the three-bin open chain omits the wrap-edge term and its covariance terms. Neither theorem as inspected states the three-bin cyclic Hessian or simplex shape results.

evidence: The uniform reference value, classical pairwise Gaussian moment machinery, and the standard half-normal boundary variance are not put forward as stand-alone discoveries. The closest ray optimizer uses two contrast edges. The cyclic objective adds a third edge whose covariances with the first two affect the derivatives.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The uniform value supplies no tangent curvature; the open-chain derivative cannot be substituted for the cyclic derivative. The extra calculation of a varying matched Gaussian covariance along the line, with permutation symmetry and interior smoothness on the simplex, supplies the negative tangent Hessian and its conflict with the boundary comparison.

evidence: In three categories the cyclic statistic is twice the range of the three matched residuals; the limit is four times the variance of the corresponding centered Gaussian range. It is not generally the range of raw counts. Under uniformity only, the matched residuals differ from the raw counts by a common shift.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The range and cyclic formulations are equivalent in the matched setting. Raw-count range results cannot be identified with the matched nonuniform statistic by a common shift. Reusing Gaussian pair formulas covers computing the variance from its covariance, not an already established extremal result for this covariance family.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A similar exact profile along the identical probability line is substantive overlap in motivation but does not give the cyclic profile or full-simplex conclusions; their different boundary values alone demonstrate different objective functions. value.rationale: Three bins are the first genuine cyclic case, have full permutation symmetry, and sit below the hypotheses of the inspected general nonuniform cyclic formula. A proved local maximum at uniformity might suggest a majorization principle; pairing its exact curvature with an explicit larger half-half boundary value decisively refutes that principle, and the ray profile also refutes quasi-concavity. This adds a structural conclusion about a natural variance family, not just a repeated uniform benchmark or a numerical slice.
residual_risks: No determination of the global optimum or extension to longer cycles is claimed.
